transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-03-16
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Emerald - Head of ML), Jose Martinez (Emerald - VP Eng), Erin Cole (Emerald - Infra)

Summary:
Quick renewal and expansion check-in. Customer interested in adding dedicated capacity, enable EU region, and discuss contract extension pricing. Talk covered performance expectations, fallbacks to hosted, security/compliance questions (SOC2, KMS), and next steps for a short benchmark and pricing follow-up.

Topics:
- Capacity upgrade options (Dedicated pool sizing, burst policy)
- Additional region onboarding (EU/Frankfurt)
- Contract extension terms and timeline
- Security: KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML, data residency
- Benchmarking and perf expectations (latency vs cost tradeoffs)

Action items (captured quickly in call): see action_items field above.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda, renewals, dedicated capacity options, and region add.
[00:12] Priya Nair: Thanks Maya. Yep, we wanted to go over numbers and timelines — we've grown volume since last quarter, and Q3 looks like a big bump.
[00:20] Jose Martinez: Hey all. From eng side we care about predictable throughput more than short bursts, so looking at Dedicated.
[00:28] Liam O'Connor: Great, we usually pair reserved capacity with burst tiers. for your workload what's your current p50 latency and token volumes?
[00:36] Priya Nair: Right now it's roughly 120ms p50 on our hosted endpoints, average 250k tokens/day, but spiking to 700k on some weekdays, and prompt sizes vary, often 400-600 tokens.
[00:48] Erin Cole: Also want to mention east EU region requirement — some customers require data to stay in EU.
[00:55] Maya Chen: Understood. We can enable a dedicated pool in eu-west-1 or eu-central depending on preference. there's a price delta for region replication.
[01:05] Priya Nair: What delta are we talking about? and is there any additional latency penalty?
[01:12] Liam O'Connor: Typical delta is ~10-15% higher unit cost due to capacity in that region and cross-region replication. latency from US users to EU region will be higher, so we'd route by policy — you can route eu traffic to eu pool and NA traffic to us pool.
[01:28] Jose Martinez: Are you able to tie latency SLAs to the dedicated pool? we're aiming for p95 < 400ms on our main chat flow.
[01:36] Liam O'Connor: We can commit to targets in a dedicated contract, yes. It depends on model variant and quantization. We'll recommend model and kernel selection for the best latency/cost balance.
[01:48] Priya Nair: Also interested in autoscale — we need predictable warmup for bursts. do you support predictable autoscale with surge capacity?
[01:55] Maya Chen: Yes, configurable autoscaling & burst capacity. you can provision baseline reserved throughput and enable a burst pool that draws down on extra capacity for short spikes.
[02:06] Priya Nair: Great. if we sign for dedicated do we have to move everything off hosted? or can we do hybrid?
[02:14] Liam O'Connor: Hybrid is common — route latency-sensitive traffic to Dedicated and keep some background jobs on Hosted to save cost. we also support automatic fallback to hosted if dedicated capacity is exceeded.
[02:28] Erin Cole: On the security side, important to confirm KMS integration and audit logs — we have to show key rotation and HSM backing for some customers.
[02:36] Maya Chen: We have KMS integrations and support customer-managed keys. our SOC2 docs and key management docs are public; we'll share links.
[02:45] Jose Martinez: Any gotchas for VPC peering / private endpoints? firewalls, subnet reqs?
[02:52] Liam O'Connor: We require a couple of dedicated subnets and specific egress rules for the control plane. we'll send the network diagram but Erin will need to open outbound to our peering IP range.
[03:04] Priya Nair: About pricing — we'd like to see a blended rate for reserved capacity plus region add-on, and an option for a 12 vs 24 month contract.
[03:12] Maya Chen: Sure. Typically 24-month commitments get a deeper discount. i'll put together 12- and 24-month pricing with expected unit economics and the EU region add-on.
[03:22] Jose Martinez: We're evaluating Anthropic and Vertex AI as well — mainly on cost and region availability.
[03:29] Liam O'Connor: Noted — we have comparative perf numbers and can show where our serving runtime and KV cache helps for large chat workloads.
[03:39] Priya Nair: Would be useful to see a short benchmark on our actual prompts. can you run a 1-hour test with our sample prompt set?
[03:46] Liam O'Connor: Yes, we can. i'll coordinate with Erin on ingress for the workload and share the test config.
[03:52] Erin Cole: i can stand up a peering test and provide a small dataset. we want to validate p95 and cost per 1k tokens.
[04:00] Maya Chen: Good. i'll include pricing options and the region add-on by Thursday. also we'll attach SOC2 + KMS docs.
[04:08] Jose Martinez: Regarding contract extension, what's the cutoff to keep current rates?
[04:13] Maya Chen: If you sign by end of March we can keep current committed pricing; after that rates may adjust with capacity cost changes.
[04:22] Priya Nair: Okay we'll try to get internal sign-off by the 24th.
[04:26] Liam O'Connor: One technical caveat: if you go with a 4k sequence model for long context, memory usage increases and costs change, we'll propose quantized variants that still meet latency targets.
[04:38] Priya Nair: Do you support on-prem private deployments? we have one regulated customer asking about air-gapped options.
[04:44] Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Private is available — usually in enterprise deals. it comes with private control plane and optional on-prem package, but licensing changes apply.
[04:54] Jose Martinez: For the benchmark, can you log kernel selection and per-token latency? we want to see bottlenecks.
[05:01] Liam O'Connor: We'll include tracing and per-token breakdown in the benchmark report.
[05:08] Priya Nair: Cool. any blockers from our side?
[05:12] Erin Cole: i'll need the network diagram and the peering IPs — i'll check with security to open the rules.
[05:18] Maya Chen: Alright, recap next steps: we'll send pricing and SOC2/KMS/network diagram, Liam will run the perf tests, Erin to provision peering test, Priya to confirm volume forecasts and internal approvals.
[05:30] Jose Martinez: sounds good. thanks all.
[05:34] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and the benchmark scheduling.

End of transcript.
